# ThreadSanitizer suppression baseline - REVIEWED per-rule ceilings.
#
# One line per rule in .github/tsan-suppressions.txt:
#
#   <rule> <ceiling>
#
# The ceiling is the number of reports that rule is reviewed to swallow. It
# is a MEASURED number with deliberate headroom, not an assertion of
# exactness: TSan report counts move with the runner's scheduling, so each
# ceiling is double the measured count, rounded up. Crossing a ceiling does
# not mean the code raced; it means the growth has not been read yet. Read
# the reports in the failing job, then raise the ceiling in a reviewed
# commit if the growth is genuine - and never in the same commit as new
# code, so the raise itself is the thing under review.
#
# The two files are one statement, checked in both directions:
#   * a rule in the suppression list with no line here fails the job -
#     rules are not added quietly;
#   * a line here whose rule is not in the list fails the job - a review
#     does not outlive its subject.
#
# The old gate compared the run's TOTAL against one aggregate cap. A total
# cannot prove that no NEW race was swallowed: a new report matching one
# kept rule can replace disappearing old reports and keep the total under
# the cap. Per-rule ceilings close that hole: growth is judged where it
# happens, rule by rule.
#
# Measured 2026-09-25, Security Hardening run 36149222233, job
# 108117967069 (the PR #81 branch, three-rule list, --test-threads=1),
# and re-measured 2026-09-27, run 36299947767, job 108565634246 after
# the dead rule was deleted (pagecache 287, arc 348, zero survivors):
#
#   race:sled::pagecache  315
#   race:sled::arc        349
#   race:sled::ivec         0  -> rule deleted as dead (it silenced nothing)
#
# Headroom policy: ceiling = 2 x measured count.
race:sled::pagecache 630
race:sled::arc 700
